Related requirements:
* 1.50.1 Verify that application documentation states the expected security features that browsers using the application should support (such as HTTPS, HSTS, Content Security Policy (CSP), and other relevant HTTP security mechanisms). It should also define how the application must behave when some of these features are not available (such as warning the user or blocking access).
* V50.8.4 Verify that the application's top-level domain (e.g., site.tld) is added to the public HSTS preload list so that the use of TLS for the application is built directly into the main browsers, rather than relying only on the relevant HTTP response header field.

"HSTS" is something to write out fully, HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS).

For 1.50.1 it is easy, for 50.8.4 it requires some wording change, because "HSTS preload list" is a term of it's own and if to write it as "HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) preload list" may not be helpful.

comments.body:
#2770 handled 1.50.1 but I want to think about the other uses as well.


| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **50.3.3** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 14.4.5] Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header field is included on all responses and for all subdomains, such as Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubdomains. | 1 |
| **50.8.4** | [ADDED] Verify that the application's top-level domain (e.g., site.tld) is added to the public HSTS preload list so that the use of TLS for the application is built directly into the main browsers, rather than relying only on the relevant HTTP response header field. | 3 |

### 50.3.3

I think 50.3.3 is getting into cheat sheet territory for no good reason, I would suggest:

| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **50.3.3** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 14.4.5] Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header field is included on all responses to enforce an HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) policy. A maximum age of at least 6 months should be defined and and for L2 and up should apply to all subdomains as well. | 1 |


### 50.8.4

If we are expanding acronyms then I think we need to do so here as well, for example:

| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **50.8.4** | [ADDED] Verify that the application's top-level domain (e.g., site.tld) is added to the public preload list for HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS). This ensures that the use of TLS for the application is built directly into the main browsers, rather than relying only on the Strict-Transport-Security response header field. | 3 |

### Glossary

I would suggest we add:

* **HTTP Strict Transport Security** (HSTS) - An policy which instructs the browser to only connect to the domain returning the header via TLS and when a valid certificate is presented. It is activated using the Strict-Transport-Security response header field.

> A maximum age of at least 6 months should be defined and and for L2 and up should apply to all subdomains as well.

Arguments and reasoning?

> A maximum age of at least 6 months should be defined

Seems like a reasonable default. We presumably need to specify something...

> for L2 and up should apply to all subdomains as well.

The `includeSubdomains` directive can be a problem depending on the application architecture so I would rather it not prevent getting to L1.

Article, last update in 2017, supports your proposal

https://wiki.mozilla.org/Security/Guidelines/Web_Security

> max-age must be set to a minimum of six months (15768000), but longer periods such as two years (63072000) are recommended. Note that once this value is set, the site must continue to support HTTPS until the expiry time has been reached.

To be able to register the domain into the hstspreload list, max-age must be at least one year

https://hstspreload.org/

> The max-age must be at least 31536000 seconds (1 year).

From a practical attack point of view, it does not matter too much, is it 2 weeks or 2 years.

Our preload requirement is L3 so we have two options:

1. Mandate 1 year from L1 and includeSubdomains at L2 
2. Mandate 6 months at L1 and 1 year and includeSubdomains at L2
3. Mandate 6 months at L1m includeSubdomains at L2 and 1 year at L3

I am thinking that maybe option 1 is best because I don't think there is much practical difference between 6 months and 1 year
For me option 1 is ok, it is aligned with requirement 50.1.1 as well (from L2 make sure that you don't have nasty room-mates).
